Class 4 · Chapter 3 of 9

Compare and use fractions

Keep track of the whole while matching parts and solving changes.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Calculate and solve step by step. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can show equal fractions.
  • I can find a fraction of an amount.
  • I can find what is left after fraction changes.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 4

Equal parts of a whole

The bottom number says how many equal parts the whole has.

The top number says how many parts are shaded.

Here 3 of 8 equal parts are shaded: 3/8.

Screen 2 of 4

Same amount, different cuts

Cut the whole into more parts and the shaded amount stays the same.

1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8.

Always keep the whole the same size.

Screen 3 of 4

A fraction of an amount

To find 3/4 of 20, share 20 into 4 equal groups.

Each group is 5, so 1/4 of 20 is 5.

3 groups of 5 make 15, so 3/4 of 20 is 15.

Screen 4 of 4

What is left?

Use 1/3 of 12 sweets. That is 4 sweets, so 8 are left.

The 8 left is 2/3 of the 12.

Follow each change to the new amount, then work out the next step.

Words to know
numerator
The top number. It counts the parts you have.
denominator
The bottom number. It tells how many equal parts make the whole.
equivalent fractions
Different fractions that show the same amount, like 1/2 and 4/8.

Chapter passed. Next: Perimeter, area and symmetry

For parents

What your child learns

Fractions can be greater than 1 and can be part of a whole shape or a quantity. A mixed number has a whole part and a fraction part. Add fractions with the same denominator by adding the numerators.

A common slip

Children often add both numerators and denominators. Keep the denominator and add only the numerators. In a grid, count the shaded parts out of all the equal parts.

5-minute home activity: Shade the whole

  1. Draw a bar and split it into 9 equal parts.
  2. Shade 7 and write the fraction.
  3. Cut 4 paper apples and give half to each of 3 friends.
  4. Count what is left and write it as a mixed number.
